theme: Bitcoin slips under $80K on Iran tensions as the Tesla-SpaceX merger push grows, AI infrastructure stocks slide on debt worries, and a Fed decision and the midterms are days away.

items.title: Bitcoin in midterm years: 2026 vs 2014, 2018 and 2022
items.picked: Bitcoin fell below $80,000 this weekend on U.S.-Iran tensions, touching about $79,000 and wiping out more than $200 million of leveraged bets in an hour. With the U.S. midterms on Nov 3, this chart lines up 2026 against past midterm years.
items.matters: Past midterm years were brutal for bitcoin because they lined up with its post-halving bear markets. 2026 has held up far better so far, which is the main pushback against 'the cycle says it's over' posts.
items.know: Indexed to the prior year-end close = 100, 2026 stood at 94 on Oct 18 (day 291), down about 6% for the year. On the same day 2014 was at 53, 2018 at 46 and 2022 at 42 (average 47), while the median of all years 2014-2025 was 154. Only three midterm years are in the sample, and the data ends Oct 18, so this weekend's drop isn't in it.

items.tab: 90 Public cos vs US ETFs BTC
items.title: Bitcoin held: public companies vs US spot ETFs
items.picked: Glassnode data making the rounds this morning shows bitcoin treasury companies have nearly stopped buying, while ETF outflows added to this weekend's selling. This chart compares the two biggest groups of institutional holders.
items.matters: Companies and ETFs each hold about 1.3M BTC, so when both stop adding at the same time, a big source of steady demand goes quiet.
items.know: As of Oct 18 the sheet has public companies at 1,304,885 BTC and US spot ETFs at 1,283,680. Companies passed ETFs at the June 30 quarter-end, and since Sep 30 they added about 8,200 BTC while ETFs lost about 8,200. Strategy's 848,250 BTC is about 65% of the company total, many companies only report quarterly, and BitcoinTreasuries.net counts a smaller 1,285,230.

items.title: Strategy's STRC buybacks as a share of weekly STRC volume
items.picked: Posts on Strategy's new capital plan this weekend point to $193.1M of STRC preferred repurchased in a single week and the buyback authorization raised to $3B. This chart shows how much of STRC's trading those buybacks make up.
items.matters: When the issuer itself is a big share of the buying, it props up STRC's price, and that matters for anyone holding the preferred for its yield.
items.know: In the week of Oct 12, Strategy bought back 1,938,780 STRC shares for $193.1M, 19.6% of the 9.91M shares traded. The record was 29.6% in the week of Oct 5, and the total since Jul 20 is 18.9M shares for $1,838.3M. The data comes from weekly 8-Ks and ends with the Oct 12 week. This image was redrawn from the sheet because the Drive export stopped at Oct 5.

items.title: US robotaxi fleets by company and state
items.picked: Tesla's Texas robotaxi fleet is nearing 1,000: Texas DMV records show about 970 vehicles, including 463 Cybercabs, nearly triple the 314 it had on Sep 1. This chart shows where that sits against Waymo and the rest of the US field.
items.matters: Tesla is growing fastest, but Waymo is still several times bigger, so this chart is the reality check for 'Tesla has caught up' posts.
items.know: As of Oct 11, the Platform Aeronaut tracker counted Waymo at 4,449 vehicles (California 1,906, Texas 1,185, Arizona 723), Tesla at 921 (Texas 739, California 164, Florida 18) and Avride at 344, out of 6,090 US robotaxis. These are tracker estimates, not company totals, so Tesla's newer Cybercab registrations aren't included, and the counts don't show how many cars run without a safety driver.

items.title: 'Musk Inc.' (Tesla + SpaceX) vs Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft
items.picked: A retail petition backing a Tesla-SpaceX merger gathered signatures covering more than 17M shares in 48 hours, after both boards set up independent committees to study a combination valued at roughly $3.5-3.7 trillion. This chart shows the two companies' combined market value against the largest stocks.
items.matters: A merged company would rank among the very biggest in the world, so this chart shows the scale of what the committees are weighing.
items.know: On Oct 20 the sheet has Tesla plus SpaceX at $3.42T ($1.48T + $1.95T), behind Nvidia at $5.22T and Apple at $4.95T and just ahead of Microsoft at $3.95T. The combined value peaked at $4.39T on Jun 16. The chart image runs through Oct 16, the data misses last week's SPCX selloff, and simply adding the two caps double-counts Tesla's SpaceX stake.

items.title: SpaceX free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex)
items.picked: SpaceX's new filing showed net income above $4B for the quarter, helped by a $561M paper gain on its Boring Company stake, as it lines up a $40B debt package. This chart shows the cash side of the same business.
items.matters: Profits look strong, but capex is soaking up far more cash than operations bring in, which explains the borrowing.
items.know: For the 12 months to Sep 30 2026, the sheet has operating cash flow of $15.8B, capex of $55.0B and free cash flow of -$39.2B. That compares with -$14.0B in 2025, -$5.4B in 2024 and +$0.1B in 2023. This image was redrawn from the sheet because the Drive export still showed the 12 months to June.

items.title: Private AI lab valuations: OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI
items.picked: Anthropic is heading toward a mid-November IPO, with reported talk of a $1.5-2 trillion valuation, even as two key Claude Code engineers announced their exits this weekend. This chart shows how fast the private AI labs' values have climbed.
items.matters: The IPO will be the first public market price on a frontier AI lab, and it will reset how investors value OpenAI, xAI and the AI chip and cloud names that sell to them.
items.know: As of Sep 2026 the sheet has Anthropic at $965B (since May 2026), OpenAI at $852B (since Mar 2026) and xAI at $250B. Anthropic was $61.5B in Mar 2025, so its value is up about 16x since then. These are reported post-money round values carried forward month to month on a log scale, and the IPO range is from press reports, not this tab.

items.title: Neocloud quarterly revenue: CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN
items.picked: IREN closed at $24.91 on Oct 23, below its 2021 IPO price of $28, while Nebius and CoreWeave slid on worries about debt and cash flow at AI data center builders. This chart shows the revenue those stocks rest on.
items.matters: Revenue is still climbing fast at CoreWeave and Nebius, so the selloff is about funding and margins, not demand. IREN's falling revenue reflects it winding down bitcoin mining before AI cloud revenue ramps up.
items.know: In Q2 2026 CoreWeave had $2,575M of revenue (up from $1,212M a year earlier), Nebius $582.3M (up from $105.1M) and IREN $137M (down from a $240M peak in Q3 2025). The data runs through Q2 and was compiled Oct 12, so Q3 results are still to come (IREN reports Nov 5), and IREN's quarters are mapped from its June fiscal year.

items.title: S&P 500 in 2026 vs the average midterm year since 1974
items.picked: With midterms on Nov 3, charts showing that the S&P 500 has risen in every November-to-June stretch after a midterm since 1942 are trending. This chart shows where 2026 sits on the usual midterm-year path.
items.matters: 2026 has bucked the usual midterm slump, so the question is whether the seasonal year-end rally still has room to run from a higher starting point.
items.know: On trading day 199 (Oct 16), 2026 stood at 111.89 (prior year-end = 100), against 97.84 for the average midterm year since 1974 and 106.27 for the average of all years. The average midterm year ends at 101.86, so it gains about 4% from this point. The data ends Oct 16, the averages hide big differences between years, and the 21-for-21 post-midterm stat comes from X posts, not this tab.

items.title: Real fed funds rate (fed funds minus core PCE inflation)
items.picked: The Fed decides on rates Wednesday, Oct 28, with 94 of 100 economists in a Reuters poll expecting a hold at 3.75-4.00% after September's hike, and September core PCE is due Thursday. This chart shows how tight policy really is once inflation is subtracted.
items.matters: A real rate just above zero means policy is barely restrictive with core inflation near 3%, which is why markets are pricing another hike in December.
items.know: In Aug 2026 the fed funds rate averaged 3.63% and core PCE inflation was 3.01%, giving a real rate of 0.62%, up from a low of 0.47% in May but down from 1.48% in Aug 2025. The data ends in August, so it misses the September 25bp hike, and it uses the monthly average effective rate.
